explanation: A function prototype describes the return type and the parameters a caller must supply. At a call, compare the number, order, and types of the argument expressions to the visible prototype.
exampleExplanation: The prototype implied by the definition takes two integers. The call supplies a value first and a maximum second.
misconceptions: A function result and its parameters describe different parts of the call.
C does not supply default arguments for ordinary functions. A variadic prototype explicitly indicates which additional arguments are accepted.

reference.title: Local C reference on prototypes and call arguments
reference.text: A prototype such as int clamp(int, int); specifies two parameters. An argument expression is supplied at the call site. A prototype using (void) specifies zero parameters. Check the diagnostic notes for the declaration the compiler used.
